fdroid:com.binauralbeat.name: Binaural Beat
fdroid:com.binauralbeat.summary: Binaural beat generator with the classic SBaGen engine and ambient backgrounds
fdroid:com.binauralbeat.description:
Binaural Beat is a binaural beat generator for relaxation, focus and sleep.
A binaural beat is created by playing two slightly different frequencies, one
in each ear. The brain perceives a third "beat" at the difference between them.
Use headphones for the effect to work.
Features:
* Two audio engines:
 - Simple: a lightweight built-in tone generator with base and beat frequency
 sliders.
 - SBaGen: the classic Sequenced Binaural Beat Generator by Jim Peters, with
 58 bundled preset sequences (brainwave states, focus levels, chakra
 progressions and more).
* Independent background layer that mixes under the beats, with its own volume:
 - Pink and brown noise, generated on the fly.
 - Looping nature samples (river, train).
* Clean, modern interface.
This is a 2026 revival of an old project: the original was a native Android
port of SBaGen via OpenSL ES. This version keeps the genuine SBaGen engine but
runs it on a modern stack.
Binaural Beat is free software, released under the GNU GPL v2. It builds on
SBaGen by Jim Peters (GPLv2). Bundled audio samples are freely licensed
(Creative Commons); see the project's CREDITS for full attribution.
Note: binaural beats are not a medical treatment. This app is for relaxation
and personal experimentation only.

fdroid:com.github.muelli.kabelwacht.name: KabelWacht
fdroid:com.github.muelli.kabelwacht.summary: A simple, free WireGuard VPN client: scan, import, and manage tunnels.
fdroid:com.github.muelli.kabelwacht.description:
KabelWacht is a minimal, fully free-software WireGuard® client for Android.
It does one thing well: manage WireGuard tunnels and connect.
Features:
* Create, list, search, edit and delete WireGuard profiles. A profile that
 can no longer be read is shown as invalid, so you can remove it.
* Import a configuration by scanning a QR code or opening a .conf file.
* Export a tunnel back to a standard wg-quick .conf file, protected by
 device authentication — the file contains your private key.
* One-tap connect/disconnect with a per-tunnel switch.
* A status notification with live traffic and the last handshake, and the
 same numbers on the connected tunnel's row. Alerts tell you when a tunnel
 fails to connect unattended, is stopped by the system or another VPN, or is
 connected but not answered by its peer. Each kind has its own notification
 channel, so Android's settings can mute or raise them separately.
* A tunnel whose endpoint is a hostname (dynamic DNS) recovers by itself when
 the peer's address changes.
* Toggle a tunnel from outside the app: launcher shortcuts, a resizable
 home-screen widget you can point at a particular tunnel, or a Quick
 Settings tile (long-press it to open the app).
* Run conditions: let a tunnel connect and disconnect by itself depending
 on the network — only on Wi-Fi, every Wi-Fi except the ones you list,
 only on chosen networks, never on mobile data or while roaming, or on
 unmetered connections only.
* Always-on VPN support, including reconnecting after a reboot.
* A structured editor with Interface and Peer sections, with the complete
 wg-quick file one tap away. It shows the tunnel's public key too, ready
 to copy for whoever administers the server.
* Fully usable with a hardware keyboard — shortcuts for search, new
 tunnel and save, and every control reachable by Tab and arrow keys.
* Userspace WireGuard backend — no root required.
Privacy and freedom:
* 100% free and open-source software (AGPL-3.0-or-later).
* No trackers, no analytics, no advertising.
* No Google Play Services or other proprietary dependencies.
* The only network connection made is your own WireGuard tunnel.
* Location permission is optional and asked for only if you set up Wi-Fi
 network-name rules, because Android requires it to read Wi-Fi names.
 Your location is never used or stored.
* Release builds are reproducible: anyone can rebuild the published APK
 from source and get the same bytes.
Built on the official WireGuard tunnel library and the ZXing QR decoder.
WireGuard is a registered trademark of Jason A. Donenfeld. This project is not
officially affiliated with or endorsed by the WireGuard project.

fdroid:com.gwitko.conduit.description:
Conduit is a local-first terminal workspace for SSH, Mosh, SFTP, and local shells.
It is built for people who need terminals from a phone without creating an account, syncing credentials through a service, or paying a subscription to open a shell.
Connect to remote machines over SSH or Mosh, browse files with SFTP, or run a full Arch Linux shell right on the device - pacman and all - with no root and no remote server.
Features:
* SSH terminal sessions
* Local Arch Linux shell on-device (Android, arm64) with pacman, running unprivileged through proot - no root, no server; downloads an Arch Linux ARM image on first use
* Mosh roaming for unreliable mobile networks
* Tmux auto attach/create per host, with start directories, prefix keys, action shortcuts, and scrollback mode
* SFTP file browsing and export
* Import SSH private keys from a file, or generate an Ed25519 key on device
* Optional passphrase encryption for generated keys, with public-key copy and export
* OpenSSH FIDO hardware-key authentication, tested with YubiKey, with multiple hardware keys per host tried in turn
* External authentication that lets the SSH server authenticate you without saved credentials
* USB and NFC support for CTAP-compatible security keys
* Saved machine profiles with tags, search, and sorting by last connected, name, or date added
* Local credential and trusted host key storage
* Trusted host key prompts and key management
* App lock with device authentication when supported
* Tabbed terminal workspace
* Customizable key row with modifier, navigation, and function keys, key repeat, latching modifiers, and your own text and control-key shortcuts
* Fullscreen terminal mode
* Terminal themes
* Background keepalive through a foreground service
Conduit does not require a Conduit account and does not use a Conduit sync service. Saved connection profiles, credentials, and trusted host keys are stored on device using platform secure storage.
Mosh support requires mosh-server on the remote host and reachable UDP ports. Predictive echo is experimental and opt-in.
The local Arch Linux shell uses tooling packaged by Termux, including proot, proot-distro, busybox, tar, xz, and supporting libraries. Conduit's own source is Apache-2.0; bundled third-party components keep their own licenses. Source-offer details are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and third_party/source-offer.

fdroid:de.ntdote.medicalcalendarlog.description:
A powerful Android application for tracking medical events, medications, and health metrics using your device's built-in calendar system. No additional accounts or cloud services required.
 🚀 Key Features 
 Quick Event Logging 
Log common medical events with a single tap using customizable template buttons. Optional dosage entry allows for precise medication tracking without hassle.
 Comprehensive Tracking 
* Health Metrics: Monitor vital signs, symptoms, and measurements
* Medications: Track drug intake with automatic concentration calculations
* General Events: Log symptoms and health-related activities
 Real-Time Drug Concentration Monitoring 
Advanced pharmacokinetic calculations provide real-time estimates of active drug concentrations in your body, helping you understand medication timing and interactions. Linear and Half-Life decay currently supported.
 Historical Data Visualization 
Interactive graphs and charts display your health data over time, making it easy to identify patterns, track progress, and share information with healthcare providers. Pan and zoomable.
 Calendar Backend Integration 
* Uses your device's native calendar system
* No additional accounts or subscriptions required
* Easy data export and import through standard calendar formats
* Seamless synchronization across devices using your existing calendar sync
* Edit and correct data with your well-known calendar tools
* Privacy-friendly calendar strongly recommended
 Smart Template System 
Create hierarchical templates where related items contribute to common categories. For example, configure beer and wine templates to both contribute to overall alcohol tracking, enabling sophisticated health monitoring scenarios.
 Intelligent Reminders 
Set up automated reminders for events that haven't occurred within specified timeframes:
* Medication adherence alerts
* Periodic health checks (blood pressure, weight, etc.)
* Routine medical appointments
* Custom health routines
 🔧 Technical Highlights 
* Privacy-First: All data stored locally using Android's calendar provider. It's as private as your personal calendar!
* No Cloud Dependencies: Can work completely offline
* Standard Data Formats: Easy backup and migration using calendar export/import
* Flexible Architecture: Extensible template system for custom tracking needs
 🔒 Privacy & Data 
Your health data can remain completely private and under your control:
* All information stored in your device's calendar
* Only transmits data to your trusted calendar backends (private calendar backend recommended)
* Easy backup through standard calendar export
* Full control over data sharing and access
 🎯 Getting Started 
1. Grant Permissions: Allow calendar access for data storage and notifications for reminders
2. Set Up Templates: Configure quick-access buttons for your most common events. Tip: use emojis as template and drug name - results in nicer graphs
3. Start Logging: Use one-tap logging for routine events, or add detailed information when needed
4. Get current status: The main screen will show you when things happened last time and how the current concentrations are
5. Monitor Trends: View your data in the graph section to track patterns over time
6. Configure Reminders: Set up alerts for important recurring health activities
Medical Calendar Log - Taking control of your health data, one event at a time.

fedora-packages:golang-github-hodgesds-p.name: golang-github-hodgesds-perf-utils-devel
fedora-packages:golang-github-hodgesds-p.description: This package is a go library for interacting with the perf subsystem in Linux. I had trouble finding a golang perf library so I decided to write this by using the linux’s perf as a reference. This library allows you to do things like see how many CPU instructions a function takes (roughly), profile a process for various hardware events, and other interesting things. Note that because the go scheduler can schedule a goroutine across many OS threads it becomes rather difficult to get an exact profile of an invididual goroutine. However, a few tricks can be used; first a call to runtime.LockOSThread to lock the current goroutine to an OS thread. Second a call to unix.SchedSetaffinity, with a CPU set mask set. Note that if the pid argument is set 0 the calling thread is used (the thread that was just locked). firefox-addons:2652981.summary: DevTools for Firefox on Android and desktop: console, elements, network, sources, Lighthouse-style audits, React, Vue, Angular and Redux/Zustand inspectors. Free, open.
firefox-addons:2652981.description:
Real developer tools on your phone. MobiDevTools adds a full DevTools panel to any page in Firefox for Android — and works just as well on desktop. Tap the toolbar button and inspect, debug and audit the page you are looking at. No computer, no cable, no adb.
 Panels 
 Console — every console message, error and promise rejection of the page, captured from the first line (works on strict Content-Security-Policy sites). Expandable objects, autocomplete on the page's real objects, top-level await, $0 / $$ / copy() / inspect(), console.table, %c styles, preserve log.
 Elements — live DOM tree with element picker; the real matched CSS rules (source file, @media, overridden declarations) editable live; computed styles and box model; addEventListener listeners with the line that added them; CSS Grid and Flexbox overlays; edit as HTML.
 Network — every request (documents, scripts, CSS, images, fetch/XHR), even those made before you opened the panel. Headers, payload, response body and JSON preview, timings, copy as cURL or fetch(), filters like status:404 or method:post, HAR export.
 Sources — all files of the page, fast even when huge or minified, one-tap pretty-print, find, snippets, download all sources as .zip. Watch expressions and logpoints.
 Pharos — Lighthouse-style audits of Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO, scored 0–100, with the exact elements to fix.
 React (and Preact), Vue and Angular — component trees, props, state, hooks, signals, Pinia/Vuex/router; edit state live. These tabs appear only on pages that use the framework.
 State — Redux, Redux Toolkit, Zustand, NgRx and every library that supports Redux DevTools: actions, state, diff, time travel.
 Application — edit localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies; browse IndexedDB, Cache Storage, manifest, service workers.
 Performance — FPS, Core Web Vitals (FCP, LCP, INP, CLS), navigation timing, slowest resources.
 For developers 
Add your own tabs with the plugin API — from an extension file or straight from your web app (window.MobiDevTools.registerPanel). The plugin guide is on the documentation website.
 Privacy 
Nothing leaves your device: no analytics, no telemetry, no remote code. The panel writes nothing into the sites you inspect, and it runs in an isolated shadow DOM that page scripts cannot read.
 Permissions 
 Access your data for all websites — to open the panel on any page you choose.
 Browser tabs and navigation — to keep the panel open across reloads.
 Network requests (webRequest) — to show the Network panel; response bodies are read-only and only in tabs where you opened the panel.
 Storage — your settings, snippets and console history.

Free and open source (MIT): https://sourceforge.net/projects/mobidevtools/

firefox-addons:2754648.name: Web Server Check Tool
firefox-addons:2754648.summary: A tool to perform basic checks on web and DAV servers.
firefox-addons:2754648.description:
This utility allows you to perform a range of tests on web and DAV servers to check their functionality. The currently supported checks are: HEAD, OPTIONS, PROPFIND, REPORT and SEARCH (in custom query only) and you can now specify your own custom query.
NB: Only HTTP and HTTPS protocols are supported and you MUST specify the protocol in the URL field.
Note: The SEARCH query is only available as a custom query and the "Depth" option is ignored as the depth should be specified as part of the query.
Known Issues:
1) Any SSL certificate errors will cause the connection to fail.
2) Only basic reporting of network errors is available.

firefox-addons:2642883.name: ARIA DevTools
firefox-addons:2642883.summary: Easily spot missing ARIA labels, misused ARIA roles, and incomplete keyboard support in your web applications.
firefox-addons:2642883.description:
Creating accessible web applications is difficult. It gets even harder if you don't understand how people with disabilities use computers.
With ARIA DevTools you see your website the way screen readers present it to the blind users. All page elements are presented according to their explicit or implied ARIA roles. This includes headings, images, tables and form items beyond others.
It's now easy to spot missing ARIA labels, misused ARIA roles, and incomplete keyboard support. This makes testing and development of accessible websites easier.
This is an Open Source project that can be found on Github: https://github.com/ziolko/aria-devtools

firefox-addons:982643.name: DevTools z-index
firefox-addons:982643.summary:
Adds "z-index" panel to DevTools. It shows ranking of elements sorted by z-index value. This would help you to reduce z-index numbers.
Stop `z-index: 999999` !!

firefox-addons:2900471.name: URL Theme Switcher
firefox-addons:2900471.summary: Automatically changes Firefox's theme color based on the current website. Handy for telling sites and environments apart.🚀
firefox-addons:2900471.description:
URL Theme Switcher changes Firefox's theme color based on the site you are visiting. Pick a URL pattern, assign a color, and the browser chrome updates when a matching page opens.
 Theme color follows the URL rules you set
 Live preview while you choose a color
 Match a whole site, a path, or subdomains
 Rules are saved and applied automatically
 English, French, German, Chinese, and Japanese
 Development, staging, and production
 Work vs personal accounts
 Spotting a service at a glance (mail, GitHub, docs, and so on)
 example.com => every page on that host
 *.example.com => that host and its subdomains
 */dashboard/* => a specific path
 Click the toolbar icon
 Choose a pattern (whole site, this page, or subdomains)
 Pick a color
 Save the rule
No data collection. Rules stay in your browser. The add-on needs tabs (to read the current URL), storage (to save rules), and theme (to color the toolbar). It does not request access to website content. The project is open source.

apple-macos:1102494854.name: System Designer
apple-macos:1102494854.description:
System Designer is a low-code development platform for creating systems.
No matter the frameworks you use and the code you write, the most important is the model that you define to create your system. 
System Designer helps you to design this model and to generate the classes and components to build your system.
DESIGN YOUR SYSTEM WITH EASE
If you look at the different JavaScript frameworks on the market, you will notice that they all have their own way to define a model, generally only with code.
System Designer uses UML, a standard, to define your model. So you probably already know how to design in System Designer even if you have never run it.
The definition of the model is stored on a JSON format called MSON. With MSON you can define types, classes, one to one / one to many relationships and multi inheritance between classes.
CODE THE BEHAVIOR OF YOUR SYSTEM
Once you have created your model, System Designer generates the skeletons of all your methods. You only have then to add your code to implement them.
System Designer provides you helpers to manage your components. You can easily navigate threw your components to create your application.
CREATE COMPONENTS GRAPHICALLY
There is no need to code to instantiate a component. Create a component in System Designer is like creating a document in a NoSQL Database.
In fact, System Designer acts as an ODM (Object-Document Mapper) to manage your components as NoSQL Documents.
RUN YOUR SYSTEM
You can run your system directly from System Designer and then export it to JavaScript, HTML, JSON or a Node.js module or a Graphviz file.
Because you have defined a model for your application, a Dynamic Type Check is done on every action of your system. All warnings are send and shown in System Designer.
DEBUG YOUR SYSTEM
System Designer can load the model of any system that runs on the browser or on Node.js. You can see the schemas, models, components and methods of the running system and you can edit them.
All modifications to the model done inside System Designer will be send to the running system. There is no need to reload to see your modifications.
DESIGN ON THE GO
System Designer can be used on macOS, iPhone, iPad or any browsers. You can also install it in your project: System Designer requires no backend to work, it is a full web application.
System Designer has a Github module to synchronize your work between all these apps. You can begin your design on your Mac and then continue it on your iPad.

flathub:dev.manufloso.sim_65c02.name: 65C02 SIM
flathub:dev.manufloso.sim_65c02.description:
65C02 SIM is a cycle-accurate 65C02 microcomputer emulator and integrated development environment
 modeled after the Ben Eater 6502 memory architecture and extended with modern retro-computing peripherals.
 Key features include:
 Full hardware simulation of the WDC 65C02 CPU, W65C22 VIA, 6551 ACIA, MOS 6581/8580 SID audio
 synthesizer, custom GPU with CRT shader support, SPI SD Card, and ESP8266 Wi-Fi interface.
 Built-in C and 6502 Assembly IDE powered by the bundled LLVM-MOS compiler toolchain, with
 live diagnostics, disassembly, and symbol inspection.
 Time-Travel Debugger, cycle-level logic analyzer, subroutine profiler, and interactive SID
 and MIDI studio tools.
 Support for distributable .65c cartridges bundling ROMs, VRAM images, and FAT16 SD card images.
